construct: Germline heterozygous pathogenic variants in RUNX1 cause an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by variable quantitative or qualitative platelet abnormalities and a substantially increased lifetime risk of myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Autosomal dominant lifelong bleeding/platelet dysfunction plus familial AML and a germline RUNX1 variant identify RUNX1 familial platelet disorder with associated myeloid malignancies.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Gray platelet syndrome, Bernard-Soulier, MYH9-related disease, and Glanzmann can produce bleeding or platelet abnormalities but do not match the germline RUNX1-associated autosomal dominant myeloid-malignancy predisposition.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The germline RUNX1 result and vertical bleeding/leukemia family phenotype eliminate competing inherited platelet disorders.
